parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
The table lists values of solubility products, $K_{sp}$, of some Group 2 carbonates.

|  | solubility product in water at $298\text{ K}$, $K_{sp}/\text{mol}^2\text{dm}^{-6}$ |
| :--- | :--- |
| $\text{MgCO}_3$ | $1.0 \times 10^{-5}$ |
| $\text{CaCO}_3$ | $5.0 \times 10^{-9}$ |
| $\text{SrCO}_3$ | $1.1 \times 10^{-10}$ |

Use the data in the table to describe the trend in the solubility of the Group 2 carbonates down the group.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.text:
Write an equation to show the equilibrium for the solubility product for $\text{MgCO}_3$. Include state symbols.

{{figure:pdf_visual_01.png}}

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: With reference to your equation in **(i)**, suggest what is observed when a few $\text{cm}^3$ of concentrated $\text{Na}_2\text{CO}_3\text{(aq)}$ are added to a saturated solution of $\text{MgCO}_3$. Explain your answer.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text: Use the data in the table to calculate the solubility of $\text{MgCO}_3$ in water at $298\text{ K}$, in $\text{g dm}^{-3}$.

parts.label: (d)(i)
parts.text:
Magnesium nitrate decomposes at a **lower** temperature than barium nitrate.

Explain why.

parts.label: (d)(ii)
parts.text:
A sample of barium nitrate was heated strongly until no further change occurred. A white solid was formed.

Write an equation for the action of heat on barium nitrate.

parts.label: (d)(iii)
parts.text:
When water was added to the white solid produced in **(d)(ii)**, an alkaline solution was produced. Adding sulfuric acid to this solution produced a white precipitate.

Write equations to explain these observations.
